title: Checks for timeout context managers which do not contain a checkpoint.
summary: Some asynchronous context managers, such as asyncio.timeout and trio.move_on_after, have no effect unless they contain a checkpoint. The use of such context managers without an await, async with or async for statement is likely a mistake. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-async and made it stable in v0.0.269.
message_templates: A `with {}(...):` context does not contain any `await` statements. This makes it pointless, as the timeout can only be triggered by a checkpoint.

title: Checks for calls to trio functions that are not immediately awaited.
summary: Many of the functions exposed by trio are asynchronous, and must be awaited to take effect. Calling a trio function without an await can lead to RuntimeWarning diagnostics and unexpected behaviour. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-async and made it stable in 0.5.0.
message_templates: Call to `{}` is not immediately awaited

title: Checks for async function definitions with timeout parameters.
summary: Rather than implementing asynchronous timeout behavior manually, prefer built-in timeout functionality, such as asyncio.timeout, trio.fail_after, or anyio.move_on_after, among others. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-async and made it stable in 0.5.0.
message_templates: Async function definition with a `timeout` parameter

title: Checks for the use of an async sleep function in a while loop.
summary: Busy-waiting for a condition in a loop forces a tradeoff between efficiency and latency: shorter sleep times improve responsiveness but waste more CPU cycles, while longer sleep times reduce CPU usage but delay reaction to state changes. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-async and made it stable in 0.5.0.
message_templates: Use `{}.Event` instead of awaiting `{}.sleep` in a `while` loop

title: Checks for uses of trio.sleep(0) or anyio.sleep(0).
summary: trio.sleep(0) is equivalent to calling trio.lowlevel.checkpoint(). However, the latter better conveys the intent of the code. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-async and made it stable in 0.5.0.

title: Checks for uses of trio.sleep() or anyio.sleep() with a delay greater than 24 hours.
summary: Calling sleep() with a delay greater than 24 hours is usually intended to sleep indefinitely. Instead of using a large delay, trio.sleep_forever() or anyio.sleep_forever() better conveys the intent. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-async and made it stable in 0.13.0.
message_templates: `{}.sleep()` with >24 hour interval should usually be `{}.sleep_forever()`

title: Checks for yield inside a context manager in an async generator.
summary: Yielding inside a context manager in an async generator is unsafe because the cleanup of the context manager may be delayed until the generator is closed, at which point await is no longer allowed. This can lead to resource leaks or other bugs. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-async. It is in preview.
message_templates: Yield in context manager in async generator may not trigger cleanup

title: Checks that async functions do not contain blocking HTTP calls.
summary: Blocking an async function via a blocking HTTP call will block the entire event loop, preventing it from executing other tasks while waiting for the HTTP response, negating the benefits of asynchronous programming. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-async and made it stable in 0.5.0.
message_templates: Async functions should not call blocking HTTP methods

title: Checks that async functions do not call blocking os.path or pathlib.Path methods.
summary: Calling some os.path or pathlib.Path methods in an async function will block the entire event loop, preventing it from executing other tasks while waiting for the operation.
